findings.summary: The fork check compares head.repo.full_name to the repository as raw strings. A deleted fork gives an empty head repo, which also takes the clean-room path. That fails closed, which is correct. GitHub treats repository names as case-insensitive, so a case-insensitive comparison would be safer against a false fork classification. A false fork classification only makes the check stricter.

findings.summary: Concurrency is now keyed on workflow_run.id, so two writer runs for the same fork branch can run in parallel. I found no way to exploit this. The write step looks up the PR head from the API (trusted), and verdict-untrusted.ts:142 refuses a record whose subject.headSha differs from that head. A comment saying that the head-match check is what makes parallel runs safe would help future readers.
